title: SaMA: Morpho Adaptation via Asymmetric Expansion of Kronecker Product
claim: The standard adapter's gauge freedom entangles optimizer axes, while our structured factorization permits only axis-aligned rescaling and gains rank faster per parameter.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, red double-arrow linking gauge-equivalent forms, rank plot at right
description: The figure has three parts. At left is the LoRA adapter. A gray W0 box is added to pink trapezoids B and A, and a second dashed box shows B, C, C^-1 and A inserted between them. A red double-arrow marks the two forms as gauge equivalent, and a green arrow points to the caption 'entangles Adam axes'. The center is the SaMA adapter. It shows W0 added to permutation-wrapped block-diagonal matrices L (blue) and R (orange), with a staircase block pattern. A second row inserts diagonal matrices D and D^-1 between permutations, linked to the first row by a red double-arrow. A green arrow points to 'axis-aligned scaling only; Adam-friendly'. At right is a line plot of adapter rank against trainable parameters. HiRA is a flat dotted green line, LoRA is a red linear line, and SaMA (Ours) is a blue curve that rises quadratically.
caption: Gauge symmetry in LoRA vs.\ \repname adapter parameterizations. (Left) LoRA's update $\Delta\rmW = \rmB\rmA$ admits any invertible $\rmC \in GL(r)$ as a gauge transform, including rotations and shearing. (Center) The block-diagonal factorization $\mP_l^\top\rmL\mP_r\rmR$ reduces the gauge freedom to diagonal rescalings only: $\rmL \leftarrow \rmL\rmD$ and $\rmR \leftarrow \mP_r^\top\rmD^{-1}\mP_r\rmR$ for diagonal $\rmD$. Unlike LoRA, this coordinate-aligned scaling does not entangle latent features. (Right) Expressivity: the rank of a \ftmt adapter scales as a quadratic function of the training budget.
abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) has attracted significant attention in the parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) landscape. However, its design suffers from two fundamental limitations. First, its invariance manifold induces flat directions in the loss landscape, creating an optimization bottleneck for adaptive optimizers. Second, its effective rank scales only linearly with the parameter budget. In this paper, we propose Scalable Morpho Adaptation (SaMA), a PEFT method grounded in a principled generalization of the Kronecker product. By relaxing the shared-block constraint in the perfect-shuffle factorization, SaMA spans from low to full rank and achieves a practical rank that scales quadratically with the parameter budget, up to full-rank. Furthermore, we show that its invariance manifold collapses to a diagonal group, making it structurally more optimizer-friendly. Empirically, SaMA consistently outperforms strong PEFT baselines on commonsense and arithmetic reasoning benchmarks while being more parameter-efficient.
